lessons.title: Rent Receipts, Rent Agreements and When You Need the Landlord's PAN

body.text: The HRA exemption is calculated from three numbers, but it is defended with documents. A correct calculation with a weak evidence file can be disallowed. A modest claim with a clean file almost never is.

children.text: Every January, HR teams send the same email: "Submit your rent proofs by the 31st or HRA will not be considered." Search results fill up with free rent receipt generators, and many employees download twelve receipts in five minutes. That habit made sense when nobody checked. Since 1 April 2026, Form 124 asks for your landlord's PAN above ₹1,00,000 of annual rent and your relationship with the landlord, and the tax department can match both against your landlord's return. This lesson shows you what a claim that holds up actually looks like.

body.caption: What a complete HRA evidence file contains

cells: That a landlord and tenant relationship exists for this home, at this rent, for this period
That the landlord acknowledges receiving rent each month
That money actually left your account and reached the landlord
Who received the rent, so it can be matched with their return
Employer via Form 124, when annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000
Whether the landlord is a parent, spouse or other relative
Employer via Form 124, from tax year 2026-27
That the rented home is the one you occupy
Tax officer: address on Aadhaar, bank records, utility or delivery bills

body.text: Receipts and agreements are documents your landlord signs, so they can be created without any rent changing hands. Bank records are the only item in the stack that is hard to fake. If you remember one thing from this lesson, pay rent through the bank.

markDefs.definition: An agreement that lets a person use a property for a fixed period without creating a tenancy with the stronger rights of a lease. It is the most common form of residential rental agreement in cities such as Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru.

children.text: A rent agreement, often drafted as a
, should name both parties, the property address, the monthly rent, the security deposit, the period, who pays maintenance and utilities, and carry both signatures. Two legal points trip people up.

body.title: Registration rules: Maharashtra vs most other states

columns.label: Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune, Thane, Nagpur and others)
points: Section 55 of the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 requires every leave and licence agreement to be in writing and registered
There is no exemption for 11-month agreements
The duty to register falls on the landlord, with a penalty for failure
Stamp duty is 0.25% of total rent and certain deposit amounts, and online e-registration is widely used

columns.label: Most other states
points: Under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, registration is compulsory for leases of a year or more
This is why 11-month agreements are so common
The agreement should still be stamped under the state's stamp law
Check your state's rules, since stamp duty rates and registration practice vary

children.text: For HRA purposes, the tax law does not demand a registered agreement. But an unstamped or unregistered agreement, where registration is compulsory, is weaker evidence and invites the question: if the paperwork was not done properly, was the rent real? For a Pune tenant paying ₹28,000 a month on an 11-month agreement, stamp duty at 0.25% on rent alone is just ₹770. It is cheap insurance.

cells: Received on 3 August 2026 by UPI, reference number

children.text: Receipts do not need to be on stamp paper. A revenue stamp of ₹1, signed across by the landlord, is needed only on a receipt for a cash payment above ₹5,000, under Article 53 of Schedule I to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899. Rent paid by bank transfer, cheque or UPI needs no revenue stamp. Online receipt generators are fine as a format, as long as every detail on them is true.

body.title: Quick Check: The Faulty Receipt
body.question: Which of these rent receipts is most likely to be rejected by an employer or questioned by a tax officer?
options: A UPI-paid receipt for ₹22,000 with names, address, month, PAN and landlord signature, but no revenue stamp
A receipt for ₹18,000 paid in cash, with all details and a ₹1 revenue stamp signed by the landlord
A receipt for ₹30,000 covering "April to March" in one line, unsigned, with no landlord PAN
A computer-generated monthly receipt for ₹12,000 paid by NEFT, with all details and the landlord's signature
body.explanation: The third receipt is unsigned, lumps the whole year together at an amount that makes no monthly sense, and has no PAN even though annual rent clearly exceeds ₹1,00,000. The first needs no revenue stamp because it was paid by UPI. The second correctly carries a stamp for cash above ₹5,000, though cash is still weaker evidence. The fourth is complete.

body.label: When you must give the landlord's PAN
body.value: Total rent in the tax year exceeds ₹1,00,000
body.context: It is the total you pay in the tax year that matters, not the monthly figure. For a full year, that is any rent above ₹8,333 a month on average.

stats.label: ₹8,333 × 12 months
stats.context: Does not exceed ₹1,00,000: PAN not required

stats.label: ₹15,000 × 7 months
stats.context: Joined mid-year, still exceeds: PAN required

children.text: Three practical points. First, check the PAN is valid and matches the landlord's name, using the Verify Your PAN service on the e-filing portal. A wrong PAN creates a mismatch for both of you. Second, in a shared flat, the threshold applies to your own share of rent. Third, if there are two co-owners receiving rent, give the PAN of each.

body.text: What if your landlord has no PAN? Under CBDT Circular No. 8/2013, issued under the old Act, the employee could instead submit a declaration from the landlord stating they have no PAN, with their name and address. It is not yet clear how employers will apply this under Form 124. Expect closer questions, and ask your landlord whether they have a PAN they have forgotten about, since most property owners do.

body.title: Try It: The PAN-Free Ceiling
body.prompt: Riya pays the same rent every month for all 12 months of the tax year. What is the highest whole-rupee monthly rent she can pay without needing to give her landlord's PAN? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: The PAN is required when total rent exceeds ₹1,00,000. At ₹8,333 a month, total rent is ₹99,996, which does not exceed the limit. At ₹8,334, it is ₹1,00,008, which does.

body.title: Quick Check: Sharing and the Threshold
body.question: Arnav shares a ₹27,000 flat in Hyderabad with two friends and pays his ₹9,000 share directly to the landlord every month. Does he need the landlord's PAN for his HRA claim?
options: No, because ₹9,000 a month is a small amount
Yes, because his own share for the year is ₹1,08,000, which exceeds ₹1,00,000
Only if the total flat rent exceeds ₹1,00,000 a month
No, because his friends are also paying the same landlord
body.explanation: The threshold applies to the rent you pay in the tax year. Arnav's share is ₹9,000 × 12 = ₹1,08,000, which exceeds ₹1,00,000, so he must give the landlord's PAN.

children.text: Circular No. 8/2013 also said employees receiving HRA of up to ₹3,000 a month need not produce rent receipts to their employer. That relief applied only to TDS at the employer's end. It never meant the rent did not need to be real or provable if a tax officer asked. Whether employers continue to apply it under Form 124 from tax year 2026-27 depends on their own policy, so keep receipts and bank records anyway.

body.title: Scenario: Twelve Receipts in Five Minutes
body.scenario: Siddharth lives with his parents in their flat in Ahmedabad and pays no rent. In January, he uses a free online generator to create twelve receipts of ₹25,000 each in his uncle's name, adds his uncle's PAN, and submits them with Form 124, describing the landlord as a relative. His employer accepts them and gives him the HRA exemption in his TDS. His uncle does not know and does not declare any rent.
body.prompt: How is this likely to come to light, and what are the consequences?
body.modelAnswer: The claim uses his uncle's PAN, so the tax department can see that ₹3,00,000 of rent was reported as paid to that PAN while the uncle's return shows no rental income. That mismatch can trigger an enquiry to Siddharth, and a notice to his uncle, who will say no rent was received. Siddharth has no bank trail, no agreement and no proof he lived anywhere but his parents' home. The exemption will be withdrawn, the extra tax charged with interest, and because he submitted false documents, he faces a penalty for misreporting income that can go up to 200% of the tax on the misreported amount. His employer's acceptance of the receipts does not protect him. If Siddharth genuinely wanted to pay rent to his parents, Lesson 9 shows how to do it properly.

columns.label: Holds up
points: Stamped, and where required registered, rent agreement
Monthly receipts with all details and signature
Rent paid every month by bank transfer or UPI
Valid landlord PAN matching the landlord's name
Landlord declares the rent in their return
Your address records match the rented home

columns.label: Falls apart
points: No agreement, or an unstamped one printed in January
One annual receipt, or receipts generated all at once
Rent paid in cash with no withdrawals to match
PAN of a relative who never received rent
Landlord's return shows no rental income
You actually live somewhere else

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Revenue Stamp
body.textWithBlank: A ₹1 revenue stamp is needed on a rent receipt only when the rent is paid in cash and the amount exceeds ₹___.
body.explanation: Under Article 53 of Schedule I to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, a receipt for money above ₹5,000 attracts ₹1 stamp duty. Payments through banking channels, including UPI, do not need a revenue stamp.

body.title: Your Monthly HRA Evidence Routine
steps: At the start of the tenancy, sign a complete rent agreement and stamp it, registering it if you live in Maharashtra or the term is a year or more
Collect your landlord's PAN and check it on the e-filing portal's Verify Your PAN service
Pay rent every month by bank transfer or UPI from your own account, with "Rent for month" in the remarks
Get a signed receipt each month, not twelve at year end
Save the agreement, receipts and a bank statement extract in one folder for each tax year
Declare the landlord's name, address, PAN and relationship accurately in Form 124
Keep the file for at least as long as your return can be reopened

body.label: Income Tax e-filing portal
body.description: Use the Verify Your PAN service under Quick Links to check that your landlord's PAN is valid and matches their name before you submit it.

cards.definition: The usual form of residential rental agreement in Indian cities. In Maharashtra it must be registered whatever its length.
Landlord's PAN is required when the rent you pay in the tax year exceeds ₹1,00,000.
A ₹1 stamp required on a receipt for a cash payment above ₹5,000 under the Indian Stamp Act. Not needed for bank or UPI payments.
An old-Act circular on salary TDS that set the ₹1,00,000 landlord PAN rule, allowed a no-PAN declaration and exempted HRA up to ₹3,000 a month from producing receipts to the employer.
Bank or UPI records showing rent leaving your account and reaching the landlord. The strongest single piece of HRA evidence.

points: An HRA claim rests on an evidence stack: agreement, monthly receipts, bank records, landlord PAN, relationship disclosure and proof you live there
In Maharashtra every leave and licence agreement must be registered. Elsewhere, leases of a year or more must be registered, and all agreements should be stamped
Receipts need names, address, amount, period and signature. A revenue stamp is needed only for cash payments above ₹5,000
Give your landlord's PAN when annual rent you pay exceeds ₹1,00,000, and verify it before submitting
Pay rent through the bank. It is the one piece of evidence that is hard to fake
Fake receipts are easily exposed through PAN matching and can lead to tax, interest and a penalty of up to 200%

Tax provisions reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026 as understood at the time of writing.
